concepts.title: Meaning and Purpose of a Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Purpose of a Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: A constitution is a written document that lays down the basic rules and principles according to which a country is governed, defining the structure of government and the rights and duties of citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Purpose of a Constitution'.
questions.a: A constitution is the supreme law that defines how a country is governed and protects the rights of its citizens.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning and Purpose of a Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Understanding the Constitution

concepts.title: The Making of the Indian Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Making of the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly over a period of about three years, drawing on discussions, debates and the study of constitutions of other countries, and was adopted on 26 November 1949.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Making of the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution was made by the Constituent Assembly through discussion and consensus, and came into effect on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Making of the Indian Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Making of the Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Constituent Assembly' refers to.
questions.a: The Constituent Assembly was the body of elected representatives that drafted the Indian Constitution, with Dr Rajendra Prasad as its President and Dr B R Ambedkar as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Constituent Assembly'.
questions.a: The Constituent Assembly, led by Dr Rajendra Prasad and with Dr B R Ambedkar as Chairman of the Drafting Committee, drafted the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Constituent Assembly' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Making of the Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Preamble and Its Significance' refers to.
questions.a: The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution that declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic and states the goals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Preamble and Its Significance'.
questions.a: The Preamble is the introduction to the Constitution that summarises its aims and the values on which the Indian Republic is built.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Preamble and Its Significance' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Preamble

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fundamental Rights' refers to.
questions.a: Fundamental Rights are the basic rights guaranteed to all citizens by the Constitution, including the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fundamental Rights'.
questions.a: Fundamental Rights are the six basic rights guaranteed by the Constitution to all citizens and protected by the courts.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Fundamental Rights' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Fundamental Rights

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Directive Principles of State Policy' refers to.
questions.a: Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines laid down in the Constitution for the government to follow in making laws and policies, aimed at establishing social and economic justice and reducing inequalities in society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Directive Principles of State Policy'.
questions.a: Directive Principles are instructions to the government to work towards social and economic justice; they are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental to governance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Directive Principles of State Policy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Directive Principles

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fundamental Duties' refers to.
questions.a: Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of citizens towards the country listed in the Constitution, including respect for the national symbols, protecting the environment, and promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fundamental Duties'.
questions.a: Fundamental Duties are the duties of citizens towards the nation that complement the Fundamental Rights they enjoy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Fundamental Duties' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Fundamental Duties

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Features of the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution is a written, lengthy and detailed document that establishes a federal system with unitary features, provides for a parliamentary government, includes Fundamental Rights and Duties, and can be amended to meet changing needs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Features of the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution is a written, federal yet unitary, parliamentary and flexible document that protects rights and can be amended.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Features of the Indian Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Features of the Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Secularism and the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: Secularism in the Indian Constitution means that the state does not promote any one religion as the official religion and treats all religions equally, allowing every citizen to profess, practise and propagate any religion of their choice.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Secularism and the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: India is a secular state where the government treats all religions equally and citizens are free to follow any religion.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Secularism and the Indian Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Features of the Constitution
